📌 Tehran, IRNA – Vice President Mohammad-Reza Aref has praised Iran’s scientific and technological achievements, saying young scientists and academics played a key role in the country’s defense during the two recent imposed wars.

Speaking at a meeting of the Science and Technology Promotion Working Group on Thursday, Aref highlighted the country’s scientific and technological advances over recent decades, saying that science, technology and academics had been at the forefront during the two recent imposed wars and that their performance in these conflicts was commendable.
​
Emphasizing that young people are among the country’s most valuable assets, he said that the enemy’s current strategy is to undermine social capital and cause social collapse through economic pressure, adding that it also has plans targeting universities.
​
The vice president added that scientific and technological advances had enabled Iran to defend itself resolutely and emerge victorious in the two recent imposed wars against an enemy equipped with the most advanced technologies, noting that the enemy had not expected Iran to possess such capabilities.
​
Aref said the country’s young scientists and specialists are the “officers of the technology war,” stressing that the government, other branches of power and national institutions must provide them with sufficient support and remove obstacles so that they can confidently and energetically advance the country’s scientific and technological development.

🌴⚓️ California, Florida, and Artificial Intelligence

Donald Trump posted a map labeling the Strait of Hormuz “New U.S. Territory.” Iran’s consulate in Hyderabad answered with a map labeling California “New Territory of the Islamic Republic of Iran.” 

The Islamic Republic has discovered the territorial-map feature.

The post was an obvious joke, but it landed during a serious dispute over Hormuz, where the United States and Iran are contesting access and control. Trump’s claim was a declaration. Tehran’s California map was a diplomatic parody of that declaration. They do not carry the same weight, even if both were designed for social media. 

Iranian state-TV commentator Mostafa Khoshcheshm proposed a less symbolic response: mining waters off Florida with “smart” naval mines. He said that would force Washington to divert military resources from the Middle East to its own coast.

That was not Iranian policy. It was a television commentator making a case for opening another front in a war already centered on a shipping route.

Meanwhile, Iran’s propaganda apparatus circulated footage said to show President Masoud Pezeshkian meeting Mojtaba Khamenei, who became Iran’s supreme leader after his father’s death. Khamenei has rarely appeared in public since taking the role. 

The footage was quickly challenged as fabricated or AI-generated. Several detection tools concluded that a photograph presented as evidence of the meeting had been altered or generated with artificial intelligence. 

The claimed meeting and the California map served different purposes. One was directed outward, mocking an American territorial claim. The other was meant for an Iranian audience, offering visual proof that the country’s new supreme leader is present and in command.

The first was a joke about borders. The second became a question about the evidence the leadership produced.
